definitions: To be overwhelmed or bogged down by excessive details or complexities, often losing sight of the main objective.
To be so involved in minor aspects of a task that progress on the overall goal is hindered.
examples: During the project, we started to be lost in the weeds with all the minor revisions.
It's easy to be lost in the weeds when you're trying to perfect every small detail.
The team needs to avoid being lost in the weeds and focus on the bigger picture.
lemma: to be lost in the weeds
source: to be lost in the weeds
